title: TAC-R2S2R verified GPU runs: 160 seeded runs of a controlled synthetic sim-to-real transfer proxy

creators.name: Li, Zipeng
creators.affiliation: School of Physics and Optoelectronic Engineering, Guangdong University of Technology, Guangzhou, China

creators.name: Chen, Jing
creators.affiliation: School of Physics and Optoelectronic Engineering, Guangdong University of Technology, Guangzhou, China

description:
Seed-level metrics, per-epoch training logs and a verification script for 160 GPU runs (4 methods × 4 source-domain budgets × 10 seeds) of a synthetic binary grasp-and-place classification proxy. The data support the paired-consistency component of the TAC-R2S2R framework described in the accompanying manuscript submitted to IEEE Access.

Evidence boundary. This is a controlled synthetic mechanism test. It is not a physical-robot experiment, not a vision-language-action policy training run, and not a complete Real2Sim2Real benchmark. The field target_success_rate is a legacy name for binary classification accuracy on target-domain samples and does not denote robot task success. No physical parameter is identified from measured data.

Contents. data/verified_runs.json (structured snapshot: 2 GPU records, 16 aggregates, 160 per-run records with confusion matrices, 10-bin calibration and full 90-epoch history); data/run_metrics.csv (160 rows); data/summary.csv (16 rows with two-sided 95% t-intervals, df=9); data/training_history.csv (14,400 rows = 160 runs × 90 epochs); data/paired_contrasts.csv; collection code (code/run_task_aware_transfer.py, self-contained synthetic-domain generator and trainer); and code/verify_numbers.py, which re-derives every headline number in the manuscript from the released files using the standard library only.

Reported hardware: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 (8.0 GiB) and RTX 5060 Ti (15.93 GiB), Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu128, CUDA 12.8. Each 80-run sweep takes roughly 75 s of wall clock.

Code is MIT licensed; data and figures are CC BY 4.0.
notes: Data-availability artifact for the manuscript 'TAC-R2S2R: Task-Aware Consistency and Residual Closed-Loop Transfer for Embodied Manipulation' (Li & Chen, submitted to IEEE Access, 2026).
